The initial moles of acetic acid are \(0.02000\ \text{L} \times 0.05\ \text{M} = 0.001\ \text{mol}\). After dilution with \(20.00\ \text{cm}^3\) water, the total volume is \(40.00\ \text{cm}^3\) and the concentration is \(0.025\ \text{M}\).

**25% titration:**  
Moles of NaOH added = \(0.25 \times 0.001 = 0.00025\ \text{mol}\).  
Moles of acetic acid remaining = \(0.00075\ \text{mol}\); moles of acetate formed = \(0.00025\ \text{mol}\).  
Using the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation:  
\(\text{p}K_a = -\log(1.85 \times 10^{-5}) \approx 4.73\)  
\(\text{pH} = 4.73 + \log\left(\frac{0.00025}{0.00075}\right) = 4.73 + \log(1/3) \approx 4.73 - 0.48 = 4.25 \approx 4.26\).

**Equivalence point:**  
Moles of NaOH added = \(0.001\ \text{mol}\). Volume of \(0.1\ \text{M}\) NaOH = \(10.00\ \text{cm}^3\). Total volume = \(50.00\ \text{cm}^3\).  
All acetic acid is converted to acetate; \([\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-] = 0.001 / 0.050 = 0.02\ \text{M}\).  
\(K_b = K_w / K_a = 10^{-14} / (1.85 \times 10^{-5}) \approx 5.41 \times 10^{-10}\).  
\([\text{OH}^-] = \sqrt{K_b C} = \sqrt{5.41 \times 10^{-10} \times 0.02} \approx 3.29 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{M}\).  
\(\text{pOH} \approx 5.48\), so \(\text{pH} = 14 - 5.48 = 8.52\).

The pH values are 4.26 and 8.52.

Answer: D
